clue.text: Equality is capital here

parts.note: par means equality, as in 'on a par'

explanation.surface: A slogan claiming the French capital is the home of equality.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface nods to the French revolutionary motto; 'here' just points at the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Paris is the capital city of France.

clue.text: Hot bread laid on, with chicken from the freezer

parts.note: a poult is a young chicken or fowl
frozen food is iced

explanation.surface: A cook layering hot bread with frozen chicken.
explanation.walkthrough: A bread poultice was a hot dressing laid on a wound; 'Hot bread laid on' defines the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To poultice is to apply a hot soft dressing, often of bread, to the skin.

clue.text: Lady queen climbs Wordsworth's mount

indicators.note: climbs in a down clue means the letters go upwards, read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
R, for Regina, is the abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: A noblewoman and a queen ascend the poet's hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbs' reverses LADY R in this down light. Rydal Mount, in the Lake District, was Wordsworth's home.
explanation.definitionFit: Rydal Mount was the house in the Lake District where the poet lived.

clue.text: Our mails sorted in the tannery

definitions.note: a place for tanning, jokily one where people tan

indicators.note: sorted suggests the letters of our mails are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Post being sorted at a leather works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sorted' rearranges OUR MAILS. 'Tannery' is used playfully: a place where people get a tan, not where hides are cured.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunroom or sunbed salon is where people go to get brown skin.

clue.text: Victory rallies round the motorway

indicators.note: round means the word rallies goes around the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: taken as written
the M1 is Britain's first motorway, written MI in crosswords

explanation.surface: A winning side regroups on either side of a motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the main motorway north from London; its letters are taken as MI.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramillies (1706) was a famous battle won by Marlborough over the French.

clue.text: Animals light up at night!

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the letters are read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: a star is a light in the night sky

explanation.surface: Creatures shining in the dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at night' only sets the scene for a star.
explanation.definitionFit: Rats are rodents.

clue.text: One's nucleus in many a book collection

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside the word many

parts.note: taken as written
I is one, plus 's
a cell is a nucleus, a small core group

explanation.surface: The central part of an anthology described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts ISCELL inside MANY.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscellany is a book of assorted writings.

clue.text: Comes down with food for Tom

definitions.meaning: alights or descends, as a bird on a perch
animal lungs fed to a tomcat

explanation.definitionFit: Alighting and offal for cats are both this word; Tom is a male cat.

clue.text: Fashionable author takes ship-to Cape Town?

parts.note: in means fashionable
Jules Verne, the French novelist
SS is steamship

explanation.surface: A fashionable writer sails to South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cape Town' looks like the South African city; it is a cape and a town in one word.
explanation.definitionFit: An Inverness is a sleeveless cape, and Inverness is a Scottish town.

clue.text: Those of experience included the burning tiger

definitions.text: Those of experience included the burning tiger

parts.words: Those of experience included the burning tiger
parts.note: Blake's collection of poems 'of Experience' contains 'The Tyger', burning bright

explanation.surface: Experienced hands recall a fiery tiger.
explanation.walkthrough: William Blake's 'Songs of Innocence and of Experience'; 'The Tyger' opens 'Tyger Tyger, burning bright'.
explanation.definitionFit: Blake's lyric poems were published under this title.

clue.text: Waves and German salute perhaps

parts.note: und is the German word for and

indicators.note: perhaps hints that salute is only one possible arrangement of its letters, so rearrange them

explanation.surface: Someone waving, and a German salute, are likened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges SALUTE into ULATES after UND.
explanation.definitionFit: To undulate is to move in waves, so undulates means waves as a verb.

clue.text: Glasgow district orders out a commercial vehicle

parts.note: 'go!' is an order sending someone out
a van is a commercial vehicle for goods

explanation.surface: A Glasgow district sends away a delivery truck.
explanation.definitionFit: Govan is a shipbuilding area of Glasgow on the Clyde.

clue.text: Supplier of topping building materials rather than toppers

definitions.text: Supplier of topping building materials rather than toppers

parts.words: Supplier of topping building materials rather than toppers
parts.note: a works making roof coverings for buildings, not the old slang 'tiles' meaning hats, which are also called toppers

explanation.surface: A firm that makes roofing materials, not top hats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tile' is old British slang for a hat, and a topper is a top hat, so the clue stresses roof tiles, not headgear.
explanation.definitionFit: A tilery is a place where tiles for roofs are made.

clue.text: Facial make-up in items like the Crossword

definitions.meaning: the parts making up a face: nose, eyes, mouth
regular newspaper items such as the crossword

explanation.definitionFit: Facial components and regular newspaper columns are both called by this word.

clue.text: Hold firearm parts

parts.note: the hammer strikes the cartridge in a gun
the lock is the firing mechanism of a gun

explanation.surface: Keep hold of pieces of a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: A hammerlock is a wrestling hold twisting the arm behind the back.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrestling grip pinning an opponent's arm behind them.

clue.text: Albums once damaged fit for the incinerator

indicators.note: damaged suggests the letters of albums once are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Old record albums, once spoiled, are only good for burning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges ALBUMS ONCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something consumable can be used up, here burnt away by fire.

clue.text: Reading from London perhaps every day

definitions.text: Reading from London perhaps every day

parts.words: Reading from London perhaps every day
parts.note: daily printed matter one reads, such as one published in the capital

explanation.surface: A commute from Reading to London each day.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading is a town near London, which tempts a commuter picture; here it is what one reads.
explanation.definitionFit: A daily publication of news, such as a London daily.

clue.text: Has this market the edge on the Stock Exchange?

definitions.text: Has this market the edge on the Stock Exchange?

parts.words: Has this market the edge on the Stock Exchange?
parts.note: a market held outside the exchange after hours, beside the pavement edge

explanation.surface: A question whether some trading has an advantage over the formal exchange.
explanation.walkthrough: The kerb market was dealing done in the street outside the Stock Exchange; a kerb is the edge of a pavement.
explanation.definitionFit: A kerb is the stone edge of a pavement, and kerb trading was unofficial dealing outside the exchange.

clue.text: Unseated spectator

parts.note: an onlooker who is on their feet, not sitting

explanation.surface: A fan who has lost their seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unseated' suggests thrown from a horse; it means standing.
explanation.definitionFit: An onlooker; read as by-stander it is someone standing by.

clue.text: It's plumb crazy art, Clive !

indicators.note: crazy suggests the letters of art Clive are jumbled wildly

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that Clive's art is completely mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plumb crazy' looks like 'plumb' as an intensifier; 'plumb' is the definition and 'crazy' rearranges ART CLIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumb means exactly upright, as a builder's plumb line shows.

clue.text: Now for the first row of the chorus!

definitions.text: Now for the first row of the chorus!

parts.words: Now for the first row of the chorus!
parts.note: the start of the day, when birds begin their morning chorus

explanation.surface: A call for the front line of singers to start.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'dawn chorus' is birdsong at daybreak; the first row is the beginning of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Daybreak is when the birds' morning song begins.

clue.text: Secretary's a male. Sue's in for replacement

definitions.note: read as 'Secretary is', with the 's as the verb

parts.note: a man is a male

indicators.note: for replacement says the letters of Sue's in are to be put back in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, with its S
taken as written

explanation.surface: An office remark that the secretary is a man, and Sue is in as a substitute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for replacement' rearranges SUES IN into UENSIS after A MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: An amanuensis is someone who writes from dictation, a scribe or clerk.

clue.text: Silence for Mrs Battle's game, when tiddly

indicators.note: tiddly means a little drunk, so the word is said with a slur

parts.note: Charles Lamb's essay 'Mrs Battle's Opinions on Whist' is about the card game

explanation.surface: A demand for quiet during a card game when someone is tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: Slurred by a drunk speaker, the card game's name gains an H. Whisht is a Scots and Irish call for hush.
explanation.definitionFit: Whisht is a dialect word meaning hush or be quiet.

clue.text: County contains a very soft sort of stone

indicators.note: contains means the word for county holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: shire is another word for a county
pp, pianissimo, is the musical mark for very soft

explanation.surface: A county is said to hold a soft type of rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapphire is a precious gemstone, typically blue.

clue.text: This law put a girl in charge (with no hope of succeeding)

parts.note: Sal is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A rule that makes a girl ruler, though she can never inherit.
explanation.walkthrough: The parenthesis is a comment: Salic law barred women from succeeding to the throne.
explanation.definitionFit: The Salic law of the Franks excluded females from inheriting the crown.

clue.text: Old king returns racing trophy inter alia

indicators.note: returns means the assembled letters are read backwards
inter is Latin for between, so one piece goes between letters of the other

parts.note: taken as written
the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: An old monarch gives back a racing cup among other things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inter alia' looks like a Latin tag; 'inter' puts TT inside ALIA to make ALITTA, which 'returns' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Attila was king of the Huns in the fifth century.

clue.text: Trust not this gate of dreams

definitions.text: Trust not this gate of dreams

parts.words: Trust not this gate of dreams
parts.note: in Homer and Virgil, false dreams come through one gate, true ones through the gate of horn

explanation.surface: A warning not to rely on a dream's doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Odyssey and Aeneid, deceptive dreams pass through a gate made of tusk, true ones through horn.
explanation.definitionFit: The gate of tusk material was the passage for deceptive dreams in classical myth.

clue.text: Such clothes could be all the rage

indicators.note: could be says rage may be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: Fashionable outfits are all the rage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges RAGE; 'all the' is padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Gear is informal for clothes.

clue.text: Arctic circle types. A slip of the tongue

indicators.note: of the tongue points to speech, so the word is said aloud

parts.note: a lapse is a slip or error

explanation.surface: A remark about Arctic people, followed by an apology for a verbal error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A slip of the tongue' looks like a set phrase; 'of the tongue' signals the homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: Lapps (Sami) are the people of northern Scandinavia, within the Arctic Circle.

clue.text: Cricket enthusiasts — how they pack the stands!

parts.note: an over is a set of six balls in cricket
a crowd of fans or supporters

explanation.surface: Cricket fans fill the stands at a match.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six deliveries from one end.
explanation.definitionFit: To overcrowd is to cram too many people in, as fans do in the stands.

clue.text: Cautious stopgap ?

parts.note: one who takes care, and a temporary holder of a post

explanation.surface: A careful temporary arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as 'care-taker' it reads as someone cautious; a caretaker government or manager is a stopgap.
explanation.definitionFit: A caretaker is an interim holder of office until a permanent one is found.

clue.text: Bird shoot in the garden

definitions.meaning: a hen kept for producing eggs
a stem pegged down to root and form a new plant

explanation.definitionFit: An egg-producing hen and a stem rooted while attached to its parent plant share this name.
